newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says thinks currencies will stabilise.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says thinks currencies will stabilise.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee meeting on Tuesday that he thinks currencies will stabilise as the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations continue their cooperation in foreign exchange markets.

He said Japan expressed its worries over excessive currency movements and told the United States, Germany and other nations during the G7 meeting in late April that it would take decisive steps against wild swings.
Japan's stance was accepted and the nations agreed to deal with excessive movements within the G7's cooperative framework, he said.
"I think currencies will stabilise. If there are any excessive moves, we will take decisive steps within the (G7) cooperative framework," Mitsuzuka said.
Mitsuzuka also said he told U.S. officials in April that the rise in Japan's current account surplus was temporary and asked them to look at the issue from a longer-term perspective.
"I think they basically accepted our request," he said.

Although Japan's economic recovery may slacken due to the April rise in the consumption tax, the economy is being steadily led by private demand, Mitsuzuka said. He said evidence of this trend will gradually appear later this fiscal year, which ends next March 31.
